title: Map as a Prompt: Learning Multi-Modal Spatial-Signal Foundation Models for Cross-scenario Wireless Localization
claim: Signal propagation differs sharply between direct and reflected paths in a structured environment, and a geographic map encodes that topology.
layout: 1 top-down map with legend bottom-left and 3D inset bottom-right
description: A top-down 2D city map plotted on X (m) versus Y (m) axes with dashed grid lines. Light lavender rectangles mark building blocks arranged in two rows with larger blocks above and below. A pink circle marks the base station. A green square marks a user equipment with a straight, pale orange line-of-sight link to the base station. A purple diamond marks a second user equipment with no direct path. A dashed blue line shows the blocked direct link. A solid blue line shows the NLoS main path, which bounces off a building corner. A legend at the bottom-left lists BS, UE (LoS), UE (NLoS), LoS, NLoS and NLoS main path. A dark-gray inset at the bottom-right shows the matching 3D building render, which is the map used to generate prompts. The eye goes first to the colored paths.
caption: Wireless propagation paths in urban environments. LoS represents direct propagation, while NLoS paths result from reflections and diffractions. Bottom-right inset: corresponding 3D map visualization showing the same LoS/NLoS topology used for prompt generation.
abstract: Accurate and robust wireless localization is a critical enabler for emerging 5G/6G applications, including autonomous driving, extended reality, and smart manufacturing. Despite its importance, achieving precise localization across diverse environments remains challenging due to the complex nature of wireless signals and their sensitivity to environmental changes. Existing data-driven approaches often suffer from limited generalization capability, requiring extensive labeled data and struggling to adapt to new scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose SigMap, a multimodal foundation model that introduces two key innovations: (1) A cycle-adaptive masking strategy that dynamically adjusts masking patterns based on channel periodicity characteristics to learn robust wireless representations; (2) A novel "map-as-prompt" framework that integrates 3D geographic information through lightweight soft prompts for effective cross-scenario adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple localization tasks while exhibiting strong zero-shot generalization in unseen environments, significantly outperforming both supervised and self-supervised baselines by considerable margins.
